battle.name: 秦鳳之戰
battle.brief: 顯德二年（955）秋末冬初，後蜀遣大將劉仁贊率眾侵入秦、階、成三州，與邊州叛軍合勢，後周世宗柴榮下詔討之，趙匡胤與諸軍自渭州西進，轉戰隴右山道，前後取階、鳳、成、秦諸州鎮，蜀軍退出隴右。卡面的斯巴達長矛並不在這條山道上：一千七百年後的隴右，靠的是唐式長槊、楯車盾牆與床子弩，而不是希臘方陣的木槍。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 這場戰爭是後周對後蜀在隴右的一場邊境爭奪，時間在後周世宗柴榮執政的顯德二年（955）秋末到顯德三年（956）初。後周一方是五代最強的中原政權：柴榮在顯德元年高平一役重創北漢之後把軍政整頓完畢，北面樞密院掌軍政，殿前侍衛司掌禁旅，州鎮設節度使與觀察使，邊防倚重戍兵與藩鎮兩套編制；出兵時往往以一鎮節度使為一路統帥，侍衛親軍充前鋒或中軍，禁軍與地方鎮兵混編。蜀方是割據成都、以孟昶為主的後蜀，前蜀後蜀的兵制基本沿唐制，宿衛有捧聖、控鶴、龍騎、虎捷一類番號，京師近衛與各州節度、縣鎮兵為骨架；蜀地鐵礦與木材充足，造甲鍛矛的匠戶集中在成都、廣漢、邛州一帶。隴右的秦、鳳、階、成四州名義上屬蜀，實際上漢蕃雜居、州縣勢力鬆散，蜀以節度使兼領防禦，周則以渭州、華州為前進基地。雙方在這條線上並非正式宣戰，而是先由蜀軍越境、叛軍響應，周廷再以收復之名出兵，因此整場衝突在正統觀裡被寫成平叛與收復，在戰略上卻是後周把刀口伸向成都盆地的第一步。
countriesEn: This war was a border struggle between the Later Zhou and the Later Shu over the Longyou region, fought from the late autumn of xiande 2 (955) into the opening months of xiande 3 (956), while Emperor Shizong Chai Rong of the Later Zhou held power. The Later Zhou side was the strongest regime on the central plain in the Five Dynasties: after crushing the Northern Han at Gaoping in 954, Chai Rong finished reforming the army and the state, with the Privy Council in the north holding military affairs and the Palace Guard Office holding the imperial troops, while the circuits and prefectures were given jiedushi and guanchashi. Frontier defence rested on two systems at once, garrison troops and regional commands, and when a campaign was sent out, a circuit commander usually led one route while the palace guard formed the vanguard or the central army, mixing guards and regional soldiers inside the same order of battle. The Shu side was the Later Shu, founded on the Chengdu plain and ruled by Meng Chang: the military system of Former Shu and Later Shu largely followed the Tang institutions, with guards organised under names such as Pengsheng, Konghe, Longqi and Hujie, the capital garrison and the troops of the circuits and county towns forming the skeleton. Shu had ample iron ore and timber, and the armourers and pole makers were concentrated around Chengdu, Guanghan and Qiongzhou. The four prefectures of Qin, Feng, Jie and Cheng in Longyou nominally belonged to Shu, but in practice Han and Tibetan communities mixed, county authority was loose, and Shu entrusted their defence to jiedushi, while the Zhou side used Weizhou and Huazhou as its forward bases. Neither side issued a formal declaration: Shu troops crossed the line first and rebellious localities answered, and the Zhou court then marched out under the name of recovering lost territory and putting down revolt. In the official account it was a pacification, yet in strategic terms it was the first step of the Later Zhou pressing a blade toward the Chengdu plain.
people: 後周世宗柴榮是這場戰爭的決策者，也是發動者。他在顯德元年高平之戰親冒矢石破北漢，之後整軍經武、取高平之利；顯德二年在北方已連敗北漢與契丹聯軍、奪回燕雲數州，正是氣候全盛之時，秦鳳之戰正是這股銳氣往西南的一次延伸，由他下詔發兵、任命統帥，並定下招撫與減賦之策。前線最著者是趙匡胤，他此時的官職在殿前侍衛司一路，位階並不高，卻奉命獨領一軍西行，在隴右山道上連下數州，戰後名望大振；後來史家談陳橋兵變，多會回頭指出他這幾年在軍中累積的資歷與人心。蜀方主帥是後蜀主孟昶的西面統帥劉仁贊，此人是蜀中宿將，奉命率眾越境、裹脅州縣，先勝後敗，兵敗被周軍擒獲，傳說解送京師處斬；他的覆亡讓蜀廷震動，也讓孟昶迅速改弦，改為主動遣使向周修貢、輸繳方物。孟昶本人並未親征，他坐鎮成都，靠的是成都至劍門、廣元、漢中、秦州這條數千里補給線調兵輸糧。史書對此役將領的姓名留下有限，除了柴榮、趙匡胤、孟昶與劉仁贊數人，多以軍號與州鎮稱呼記錄；這種記法本身就說明戰役規模不大，而戰果來得很快。
peopleEn: Chai Rong, Emperor Shizong of the Later Zhou, was the decision maker and the man who started this war. He had personally taken the field at Gaoping in 954 and broken the Northern Han, then reformed the army and the state, harvesting the advantage of that victory; by xiande 2 he had already beaten the Northern Han and the Khitan coalition in the north and taken back several prefectures of the Yan-Yung region, and this was the high point of his momentum, so the Qin-Feng war was that momentum extended to the southwest. He issued the orders to march, appointed the commanders, and set the policy of amnesty and reduced levies. The most prominent man on the ground was Zhao Kuangyin. His post at that time was in the Palace Guard Office, not a high rank, yet he was given a single army to lead westward, and he took several prefectures in a row along the mountain roads of Longyou, which raised his renown sharply afterwards; when later historians discuss the Chenqiao mutiny they often look back at the standing and the network he had built in the army over those years. The Shu commander was Liu Renzan, the western commander of the Later Shu ruler Meng Chang. He was a veteran of the Shu army, sent across the border with troops to seize or bully the local prefectures into joining, winning first and losing later, and being taken by the Zhou troops when his army broke; the story is that he was carried to the capital and executed. His collapse shocked the Shu court and pushed Meng Chang to change tack at once, sending envoys to pay tribute to Zhou and hand over local products. Meng Chang himself never came to the field; he stayed in Chengdu and drew on the supply line running from Chengdu through Jiange, Guangyuan, Hanzhong to Qin Prefecture, thousands of li long, to move troops and grain. The histories preserve very few names of the officers in this campaign: apart from Chai Rong, Zhao Kuangyin, Meng Chang and Liu Renzan, the record speaks in unit titles and prefectural names, and that way of recording is itself a sign that the campaign was not large and that its results came quickly.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是斯巴達長矛：兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套，屬於古希臘重裝步兵方陣的核心器械，公元前五至四世紀的希臘城邦以它和圓盾組成密集陣線。它在秦鳳的戰場上並不存在——九百五十五年的隴右，沒有任何一支軍隊使用希臘式長矛，也沒有那種以圓盾密排、層層互相遮蔽的方陣；長矛這一路形制在西方也已退場，只在拜占庭重裝步兵那樣的單位裡留下較短、較粗的刺槍與塔盾的影子。真正出現在隴右山道上的是唐式長柄兵器：蜀軍的槊、戟、刀，與後周的長槊、陌刀，木柄或鐵柄，格為刃部，刺穿力來自臂力與槊鋒而非配重。蜀步軍還大量使用楯車、拒馬與鹿角，把車欄與長槊排成可以互相頂住的車牆，結構上與希臘方陣的盾線同源，思路同樣是用前排的身體與器械替後排的刀槊開路，但器械與訓練完全不同。除長柄兵器外，兩軍都備弓弩、唐代明光鎧一類的鎧具與拒馬鹿角，攻城一方還帶發石車一類的投石器、床子弩與雲梯；後蜀地處蜀道，兵員補充與糧秣極難跨越劍門天險，這正是其攻勢只能維持半年的原因。馬匹方面，蜀地不產北地那樣的戰馬，騎兵比例低而以突騎、游騎的游鬥為主；後周的禁旅精騎與北地邊軍則有較完整的馬甲與長刀，戰馬數量也佔優。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Spartan dory: a wooden spear two metres long with a bronze butt cap, the central arm of the phalanx of the ancient Greek hoplite, used in the fifth and fourth centuries BC by the city-states of Greece to build a dense line together with the round shield. It did not exist on the field at Qin-Feng. In Longyou in the year 955 no army used a Greek-style long spear, and there was no phalanx of round shields pressed together and shielding each other layer by layer; the long spear line had already left the western battlefield, surviving only in the shadow of the shorter, thicker thrusting spear and the tower shield of units such as the Byzantine cataphraktoi. What actually appeared on the mountain roads of Longyou were Tang-style pole arms: the shao, halberd and sabre of the Shu troops, and the long shao and the modao of the Later Zhou, with wooden or iron shafts, a distinct blade section, and their piercing power coming from arm strength and the point of the shao rather than from any counterweight. Shu infantry also used large numbers of shield carts, cheval-de-frise and deer-horn obstacles, lining the cart rails and long spears into a wall that could hold the enemy off; structurally this is the same idea as the shield line of a Greek phalanx, using the bodies and equipment of the front rank to open a path for the blades of the rank behind, but the gear and the training are entirely different. Besides the pole arms both sides carried bows and crossbows, armour of the Tang bright-plated type, and cheval-de-frise and deer-horn obstacles, while the besieging side brought stone-throwers of the traction type, bed crossbows and scaling ladders. Shu stood inside the Shu roads, where replacements and grain could hardly cross the barrier of Jiange, which is exactly why its offensive could last only half a year. On horses, Shu did not breed the warhorses of the northern plains: its mounted proportion was low and it relied on the skirmishing of the tuqi and youqi, while the elite guard cavalry and the northern frontier troops of the Later Zhou had fuller caparisons and sabres and held the advantage in numbers of horses.
tactics: 後周的戰法是典型的五代邊疆攻勢：先以一軍駐渭州作前進基地，整備糧秣、徵發民夫治河築橋，再分兵出塞；大軍沿渭河北岸西行，過成紀、翻隴阪，攻擊的重點是蜀軍防禦相對薄弱的階、鳳、成三州，而不是蜀師集結的秦州城牆。趙匡胤所領的一路以禁軍精騎為先鋒，步兵繼之，遇到蜀軍拒馬與車牆時，先以弩箭、擲石在遠距離壓制，等蜀陣被扯出缺口才以長槊壓上；遇到城池則改用穴地與雲梯，逼近城牆後以櫓車蔽身衝撞，試圖在城下的短兵接觸中取勝。蜀方的守禦依托秦鳳一帶的山水之險：鳳州在嘉陵江與渭水之間的高坡，階、成兩州卡在白龍江與西和水的谷口，州城多依山築堡，防守方居高臨下，用弓弩與擲石封住谷道；蜀軍還在城郊列楯車拒馬，企圖以車牆和長槊頂住周軍衝鋒，關鍵在於能否守住谷口狹窄的地帶。整場戰役的勝負手其實不在單城池攻防，而在雙方補給線的長短：周的糧食從關中及中原運來，距離較短；蜀的糧食要從成都盆地翻越大巴山、穿劍門、沿嘉陵江谷北上，數千里山地驛程，士卒的食糧、軍械與援兵到達速度都受制於蜀道天險，冬春之際山地缺糧，軍心與士氣被拖得很快。卡面那支斯巴達長矛所代表的方陣戰法，在這條補給線面前毫無作用。
tacticsEn: The Later Zhou used the typical Five Dynasties frontier offensive: first a detachment was stationed at Weizhou as the forward base, with grain and supplies sorted out and corvée labourers repairing the river and building bridges, and only then were the columns sent out. The main body moved west along the north bank of the Wei river, passed Chengji and climbed the Long slopes, and struck at Jie, Feng and Cheng, where the Shu defence was thin, rather than at the walls of Qin Prefecture where the Shu army was massed. The route Zhao Kuangyin led used elite guard cavalry as its vanguard with infantry behind it; when it met Shu cheval-de-frise and cart walls it first pressed at range with crossbow bolts and thrown stones, and only drove the long shao home once a gap had been torn in the Shu line. Against walled towns it changed to mining and scaling ladders, and once close to the wall it tried to ram with covered carts, seeking the decision in close fighting below the rampart. The Shu defence leaned on the terrain of the Qin-Feng region: Feng Prefecture sat on a high slope between the Jialing and the Wei, while Jie and Cheng lay in the valleys of the Bailong and the Xihe rivers, their county towns built as fortresses against the hillside so that the defenders could look down and seal the passes with bows and thrown stones. The Shu also lined shield carts and obstacles outside the towns, hoping to hold the Zhou charge with a wall of carts and long spears, and the key question was whether the narrow ground at the mouth of the valley could be kept. The real hinge of the campaign lay not in the assault on any single walled town but in the relative length of the two supply lines. Zhou grain came from Guanzhong and the central plain, a short run. Shu grain had to leave the Chengdu plain, cross the Daba mountains, pass Jiange and come north up the Jialing valley, a journey of thousands of li over mountain roads, and the speed at which food, weapons and reinforcements arrived was governed entirely by the difficulty of the Shu roads; in winter and spring the mountains ran short of grain, and morale drained away quickly. The phalanx fighting that the Spartan dory on the card stands for was of no use whatsoever against a supply line like that.
data: 關於兵數，兩部史書都只給出量級而沒有確數：蜀軍入侵時以劉仁贊為首，記載多作率眾數萬；周軍出動的是一整路兵，趙匡胤所領者以禁軍與邊鎮兵混編，人數同樣落在數萬量級。時間上，蜀軍越境與周廷下詔在顯德二年（955）秋末冬初，戰事在冬季的隴右展開，到翌年顯德三年（956）初四州平定。距離上，從渭州（今甘肅平涼）到秦州（今甘肅天水）沿渭水直線約二百五十公里，但軍隊實際走的是渭河谷與隴阪山道，迂迴而多險；秦州與鳳州相距約一百公里，階州在秦州西南、成州在更南的谷地裡，蜀道最窄處僅容車馬單行。損失方面，蜀軍被斬、被俘與潰散的數目，各家記載從數千到數萬都有，較可確認的是蜀軍主力在階、鳳之間的一役中崩潰，周軍隨後連取數州；周軍自身亦有相當傷亡，記載提到趙匡胤一軍出隴時人數較出發時減少。糧秣與物資方面，隴右是產馬、產鐵、產木之地，蜀的物資須靠劍門棧道北運，周的物資靠關中與中原供應；戰後秦鳳四州按詔免租、招撫流亡，州縣重新編戶。
dataEn: On numbers, the histories give orders of magnitude rather than exact figures. When the Shu army crossed the border under Liu Renzan the records usually say he led several tens of thousands of men. The Zhou force sent out was a full route army, and the part Zhao Kuangyin led mixed guard troops with frontier soldiers, again in the tens of thousands. In time, the Shu incursion and the Zhou order to march belong to the late autumn and early winter of xiande 2 (955); the fighting unfolded in Longyou through the winter, and by the opening of xiande 3 (956) the four prefectures had been settled. In distance, the straight line down the Wei from Weizhou (today Pingliang in Gansu) to Qin Prefecture (today Tianshui in Gansu) is about 250 kilometres, but the armies actually used the Wei valley and the Long slopes, a roundabout and hazardous road. Qin and Feng are about a hundred kilometres apart, Jie lies south-west of Qin and Cheng further south down the valleys, and at its narrowest the Shu road allows only a single file of horses and carts. On losses, the figures for Shu men killed, captured or scattered run from several thousand to tens of thousands, and what can be confirmed is that the main Shu force collapsed in one action between Jie and Feng, after which the Zhou took several prefectures in succession. The Zhou army also lost a substantial number of men, and the record notes that Zhao Kuangyin's force was smaller on leaving Longyou than when it set out. On supplies and materiel, Longyou produced horses, iron and timber; Shu materiel had to be carried north through the plank roads of Jiange, while the Zhou drew on Guanzhong and the central plain. After the war the four prefectures of Qin and Feng were granted remission of tax by decree, the displaced were called back, and the counties were enrolled once more.
cause: 秦鳳之戰的直接起因是後蜀越境與邊州響應。顯德二年，後周正全力對付北漢與契丹，人力有限；蜀主孟昶看準這個窗口，命西面大將劉仁贊率眾自秦州方向向北推進，奪取秦、鳳、階、成之間的關鍵渡口與山寨，把周方在隴右的前哨擠到渭水一線。同時，蜀境內與中原王朝久有爭議的秦鳳各州，漢蕃部眾與州鎮軍將各懷心思，蜀軍一到便有州縣望風響應，這使後周有了邊州叛亂、蜀軍助逆的出兵口實。更深一層的原因是後周的整體戰略：柴榮在北方已取得高平與遼南之勝，剩下的硬骨頭是盤踞成都平原的後蜀；蜀若據有秦鳳，向東可窺渭州、華州，向北可援河東，向西可聯吐蕃與唃廝，是周側翼上最不穩的一根釘子。反過來看，蜀也有不得不動的理由：從唐末到五代，秦鳳一帶反覆易主，蜀對這四州的控制並不牢固，州將往往只知擁兵自重，一旦中原主力南下，蜀必須先保住關口。後周之所以用兵而不只是外交施壓，是因為它清楚蜀的弱點在補給——只要把戰線推到隴右山道深處，蜀的遠征能力就會被距離拖垮。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the Qin-Feng war was the Shu crossing the border and the border prefectures answering the call. In xiande 2 the Later Zhou was fully occupied with the Northern Han and the Khitans and had little manpower to spare. Meng Chang of Shu saw the opening and ordered the western commander Liu Renzan to push north from the Qin direction with a body of troops, to seize the key fords and stockades between Qin, Feng, Jie and Cheng and to squeeze the Zhou outposts in Longyou back to the line of the Wei river. At the same time, the Qin-Feng prefectures had long been disputed between Shu and the central plain dynasties; the Han and Tibetan populations and the military governors of the counties each had their own interests, and when the Shu troops arrived some counties and prefectures answered the call, which gave the Zhou a pretext for intervention in the shape of revolt in the border prefectures aided by Shu troops. At a deeper level there was the overall strategy of the Later Zhou. Having won at Gaoping and in the south of Liao territory, the remaining hard nut for Chai Rong was the Later Shu sitting on the Chengdu plain. If Shu held Qin and Feng it could look east at Weizhou and Huazhou, reach north towards Hedong, and link up with the Tibetans and the Dangxiang peoples to the west; it was the most unstable nail in the Zhou flank. In turn Shu had its own reasons for moving. From the end of the Tang through the Five Dynasties the Qin-Feng region changed hands again and again, and Shu's grip on those four prefectures was never firm; the county commanders were often more interested in keeping their own men than in obedience, so once the central plain moved its main force south, Shu had to hold its passes first. The reason the Zhou used the sword rather than mere diplomatic pressure was that it knew where Shu was weak, in its supply: push the line deep into the mountain roads of Longyou and the Shu's ability to project force would be dragged apart by distance.
impact: 這場戰役的直接後果，是後蜀失去整個隴右。蜀退出秦、鳳、階、成四州，疆域退守成都平原，兩國邊界從隴山東麓退到劍門與大巴山一線；蜀的北面屏障由天險變成通道，此後再想北進，就必須走蜀道最難走的一段。對後周而言，四州入版之後，隴右的馬匹、鐵料、鹽與木材納入中原王朝的資源版圖，渭水上游的軍鎮可以互相照應，西南方向再無後顧之憂；後周在四州置軍置縣、招撫流亡、免除數年賦役，把剛打下來的邊地重新編入戶籍，隴右的漢蕃部落在唐末五代長期的戰亂中第一次出現較穩定的州縣秩序。對宋而言，這一仗是通往滅蜀的地理鋪墊：後周世宗顯德六年（959）北征途中病逝，幼主即位，軍權很快被趙匡胤一系接過，後周對蜀的戰事半途而廢，隴右的經營在宋初延續，十八年之後（965）宋軍才真正沿著同樣的山道滅蜀，分割了後蜀。對趙匡胤本人，這場戰役是他十年間累積的軍功之一：他在隴右以年輕將領的身份獨當一路，隨後在陳橋被部下推舉時，願意支持他的人都清楚他能打這件事並非虛名。對後蜀而言，這是一次失去北伐能力的轉折，孟昶此後再無力重啟對中原的戰端，只剩年年納貢的屈辱與逐步加深的內部問題。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the campaign was the loss of all of Longyou by the Later Shu. Shu withdrew from the four prefectures of Qin, Feng, Jie and Cheng, its territory contracting to the Chengdu plain, and the frontier between the two states pulled back from the eastern foot of the Long mountains to the line of Jiange and the Daba range. The barrier on Shu's northern side turned from a natural defence into an approach road; from then on, to strike north it had to take the hardest stretch of the Shu roads. For the Later Zhou, once the four prefectures were in hand the horses, iron, salt and timber of Longyou entered the resources of the central plain dynasty, the garrisons on the upper Wei could support one another, and the southwest no longer sat behind a worrying flank. The Zhou established military posts and counties in the four prefectures, called back the displaced, and remitted the levies of several years, folding the newly conquered borderland back into the registers; in the long disorder of the late Tang and the Five Dynasties, the Han and Tibetan communities of Longyou saw their first relatively stable county order in a long while. For the Song this battle was the geographic preparation for destroying Shu: in xiande 6 (959) the Later Zhou emperor fell ill and died on a northern campaign, the child sovereign succeeded him, and military power quickly passed into the hands of Zhao Kuangyin's group, so the Zhou war against Shu was abandoned halfway, and the administration of Longyou continued into the Song, which only in 965 marched along the same mountain roads to end Shu for good. For Zhao Kuangyin himself the campaign was one of the military credits accumulated over a decade: he had led a route of the army alone in Longyou as a young general, and when his men raised him at Chenqiao, those ready to follow him knew that his reputation for fighting was not an empty claim. For Shu it was a turning point that cost it the ability to mount a northern offensive; Meng Chang never again had the strength to reopen the war against the central plain, leaving only the humiliation of annual tribute and a deepening of internal problems.
result: 結果是後周全勝：蜀軍退出隴右，秦、鳳、階、成四州及沿線軍鎮全部歸於後周，蜀方在西北方向的據點被連根拔除。前蜀後蜀盤踞成都近六十年，到孟昶手上被削去北翼，只剩益、梓、黔、忠諸州與劍門以南的山地；四州易主之後，蜀主孟昶不再有北伐的念頭，改而向後周稱臣納貢，維持表面上的和平，這種委曲求全的狀態一直延續到宋太祖即位、太平興國年間統一江南之後。戰役本身規模不算大，歷時約半年到一年，參戰兵員在數萬量級，沒有決定性的會戰，也沒有巨大的攻城損失；它之所以重要，是因為雙方都知道下一場衝突的規模會更大，而蜀在這一次交鋒裡先露出兩個致命弱點：隴右的縱深不足，以及從成都盆地往北投送兵力的距離太長。對後周來說，取四州還意味著往後可以從西面包抄南唐與江南，而不必擔心背後有蜀軍；對後蜀來說，輸掉秦鳳之後只能退回山谷裡死守劍門，等到宋軍真的沿著秦鳳的山道推進時，它已沒有多餘的縱深可用。至於卡面那支斯巴達長矛，它在這場戰爭裡沒有出現，也不必出現：秦鳳的山道考驗的是糧秣、騎兵與耐力，而不是方陣的厚度。
resultEn: The outcome was a complete Later Zhou victory: the Shu army withdrew from Longyou, and the four prefectures of Qin, Feng, Jie and Cheng with the garrison towns along the line passed entirely to the Later Zhou, cutting away the Shu bases in the northwest. Former Shu and Later Shu had held the Chengdu plain for close to sixty years, and under Meng Chang the northern wing was lopped off, leaving only the prefectures of Yi, Zi, Qian and Zhong and the mountains south of Jiange. Once the four prefectures changed hands, Meng Chang gave up the thought of a northern offensive and turned instead to acknowledge the Zhou as overlord and pay tribute, keeping up a surface peace; that back-and-pedalling lasted until the Song founder came to the throne and the south was unified in the Taiping Xingguo years. The campaign itself was not large. It ran for roughly half a year to a year, the troops involved were in the tens of thousands, there was no single decisive battle and no enormous siege loss. Its importance lay in the fact that both sides knew the next clash would be far bigger, and that Shu in this encounter showed two fatal weaknesses: insufficient depth in Longyou, and a distance for feeding an army north from the Chengdu plain that was simply too long. For the Later Zhou, taking the four prefectures also meant that in future it could approach the Southern Tang and the Jiangnan from the west without worrying about Shu troops at its back. For Shu, losing Qin and Feng meant it could only fall back into the valleys and hold Jiange, and when the Song army really came along the Qin-Feng roads it had no depth left to spend. As for the Spartan dory on the card, it did not appear in this war and did not need to: the roads of Qin-Feng tested grain, cavalry and endurance, not the thickness of a phalanx.
